findings.subject: Implementation
findings.title: Correlation/trace IDs are not propagated into structured logs across the request lifecycle

evidence.excerpt: catch (Exception exception) { var loggingCorrelation = LoggingUtilities.GetLoggingCorrelation(); this.logger.LogError(exception, "{UserMessage}", loggingCorrelation.UserMessage);

findings.standard: OpenTelemetry — correlating logs, traces and metrics
findings.recommendation: Enrich Serilog output with the active OpenTelemetry trace/span IDs (e.g. via Serilog.Enrichers.Span, or by pushing Activity.Current?.TraceId/SpanId into LogContext in middleware) so every log line — not just unhandled-exception logs — carries the same correlation identifier as the corresponding distributed trace, and ensure that identifier is preserved across any async/queue boundaries. LoggingCorrelation currently mints an unrelated new GUID only when an unhandled exception occurs, so it cannot be used to correlate a request's logs with its trace in the normal, non-error path.

checkResults.subject: Implementation
checkResults.reason: Serilog enrichers do not attach the OpenTelemetry trace/span ID (or any other stable correlation ID) to log events; the only correlation ID in the codebase is a fresh GUID minted solely on unhandled exceptions, unrelated to the request's actual trace ID, so logs, traces and metrics for the same request cannot be joined.

checkResults.subject: Implementation
checkResults.reason: No SLO/SLI documentation found in docs/, README.md or elsewhere in the repository; only a general 'Health Check: Basic health check endpoint' feature bullet is mentioned, with no latency/error-rate/availability targets.

notes: OBS-06 passes on existence (an anonymous /healthcheck endpoint returns 200 OK), but note it is a bare liveness ping — it does not use ASP.NET Core's AddHealthChecks()/MapHealthChecks() and performs no dependency checks (e.g. SQL Server/PostgreSQL connectivity), so it cannot distinguish 'process is up' from 'app is actually ready to serve'. No languages/csharp.md exists under review-observability/references, so only the shared checklist was applied.
